subQuestions.questionText: The compartment in the ruminant stomach that has folds that increase the total surface area for absorption of water:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
The omasum has many folds (leaves/laminae) that greatly increase its surface area for the absorption of water and minerals from digesta in ruminants.

subQuestions.questionText: … is an example of a fat-soluble vitamin that is essential for normal reproduction.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin essential for normal reproduction. The B-vitamins (B1, B6, B12) are water-soluble.

subQuestions.questionText:
Each of the following is a requirement for a feed flow programme:
(i) Matches feed production capabilities of the farm to the animal feed requirements
(ii) Ensures negative margin over feed cost
(iii) Makes feed available to animals throughout the production period
(iv) Ensures sustainable use of resources

Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
(i), (iii) and (iv) are correct. Statement (ii) is wrong because a feed flow programme aims for a positive margin over feed cost, not a negative one.

subQuestions.questionText: Feeds with proteins of high biological value are used for …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Proteins of high biological value contain essential amino acids needed for tissue building and reproduction. They are therefore used for growth and reproduction.

subQuestions.questionText: A sign of aggressive behaviour in cattle:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Pawing the ground is a typical aggressive sign in cattle. Drooping head/ears, slow movement, and reluctance to get up are signs of illness, not aggression.

options.C: Lying down and reluctant to get up

subQuestions.questionText:
The statements below describe an extensive production system:
(i) A small number of animals on a huge area of land
(ii) Little human involvement and technological input
(iii) High production output
(iv) Animals fend food for themselves

Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
(i), (ii) and (iv) describe an extensive production system. Statement (iii) is incorrect — extensive systems have LOW production output per animal/area, not high.

subQuestions.questionText: An instrument that is used to administer the deworming liquid to sheep:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
A dosing gun is the specific instrument used to administer liquid dewormers (drenches) orally to sheep. A burdizzo is for castration, a scalpel for cutting, and 'dewormer' is the medicine itself, not the instrument.

subQuestions.questionText: Metabolic diseases are caused by mineral deficiencies and are ...
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Metabolic diseases are caused by nutritional/mineral deficiencies and are non-infectious — they cannot be transmitted from one animal to another.

subQuestions.questionText: The membrane surrounding the foetus and responsible for the removal of urine:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
The allantois is the foetal membrane responsible for the storage and removal of urine/foetal waste. The amnion contains amniotic fluid, the chorion is the outermost membrane, and the placenta facilitates nutrient exchange.

subQuestions.questionText: ONE of the following statements with regard to the normal lactation of dairy cows is INCORRECT:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Statement B is INCORRECT. The relationship is inverse: the higher the milk yield, the LOWER the butterfat content (not higher). Statements A, C and D are all correct.

options.A: The higher the milk yield, the lower the butterfat content.
options.B: The higher the milk yield, the higher the butterfat content.
options.C: The period of milk production in cows is approximately 305 days.
options.D: Milk production drops before drying up.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE.
A: Concentrates / B: Roughages
Description: Provide bulkiness to the ration of a ruminant farm animal
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B only (2 marks)
Roughages provide bulkiness/fibre to the ration of ruminants. Concentrates are nutrient-dense and low in fibre, so they do not provide bulkiness.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE.
A: Hindgut fermentation / B: Rumen fermentation
Description: Digestion facilitated by microorganisms found in the alimentary canal
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Both A and B (2 marks)
Both hindgut fermentation (in the caecum/large intestine of horses, rabbits) and rumen fermentation (in ruminants) are facilitated by microorganisms (bacteria, protozoa, fungi) in the alimentary canal.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE.
A: Nipple drinkers / B: Computerised feeding troughs
Description: Supply water to pigs in an intensive production system
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A only (2 marks)
Nipple drinkers supply water to pigs in intensive systems. Computerised feeding troughs supply feed (not water).

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE.
A: Soil sods / B: Wood shavings
Description: Used in pens to absorb the moisture and insulate cold cement floors
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B only (2 marks)
Wood shavings are used as bedding material in pens to absorb moisture and insulate against cold cement floors. Soil sods are used to supplement iron in piglets.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE.
A: Antibiotics / B: Glycerol
Description: Protect semen against pH changes
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: None (2 marks)
Neither antibiotics nor glycerol protects semen against pH changes. Antibiotics prevent bacterial growth; glycerol acts as a cryoprotectant during freezing. Buffers (e.g. citrate, phosphate) protect against pH changes.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term for the following description: The process whereby the partially digested stomach content is returned to the mouth for further chewing.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2: Regurgitation (accept retro-peristalsis)
[Award 2 marks for either correct term]

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term for the following description: A preventative measure whereby animals with a contagious disease are kept away from healthy animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2: Quarantine (accept isolation)
[Award 2 marks for either correct term]

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term for the following description: A common canal in male animals that is used for excretion of urine and semen.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2: Urethra
[Award 2 marks for the correct term]

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term for the following description: An organelle in the head of a sperm cell which contains genetic materials.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2: Nucleus
[Award 2 marks for the correct term]

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term for the following description: A condition where female animals are unable to conceive after several attempts of artificial insemination.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1-2: Repeat-breeder syndrome
[Award 2 marks for the correct term]

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make the statement TRUE: 'Chyme' is food that is ball-like and which is mixed with saliva in the mouth of an animal during digestion.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Bolus
[Award 1 mark — bolus is the correct term for food mixed with saliva and formed into a ball in the mouth. Chyme refers to food after stomach digestion.]

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make the statement TRUE: Farming where crops and livestock are produced and sold on a large scale for profit, is called an 'intensive' farming system.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Commercial
[Award 1 mark — commercial farming is large-scale production for profit. Intensive farming refers to high input/output per area, which is a different classification.]

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make the statement TRUE: The 'sheath' encloses the primary male reproductive organ.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Scrotum
[Award 1 mark — the scrotum encloses the testes (the primary male reproductive organs). The sheath/prepuce encloses the penis.]

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make the statement TRUE: 'Maceration' occurs when the placenta, together with liquids, dries out and only a hard dried foetus remains in the uterus.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Mummification
[Award 1 mark — mummification is when the foetus dries out and remains in the uterus as a hard mass. Maceration is the breakdown/disintegration of foetal tissues.]

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make the statement TRUE: A powerful contraction of the muscles during mating resulting in the deposition of semen into the vagina of a cow is known as 'secretion'.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Ejaculation
[Award 1 mark — ejaculation is the powerful muscle contraction that deposits semen into the female reproductive tract during mating.]

subQuestions.questionText: Name the farm animal represented by the alimentary canal in the diagram. (Refer to the diagram of the alimentary canal showing parts A, B, C, D, E in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Chicken (accept fowl/poultry)
[Award 1 mark for any correct identification]

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons, which are visible in the diagram, to support the answer to QUESTION 2.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Presence of a crop
• Presence of proventriculus/glandular stomach
• Simple stomach/monogastric
• Presence of ventriculus/gizzard/muscular stomach
• Presence of caeca/two blind guts
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the pH of the contents of each of the following parts:
(a) B
(b) E
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) B - Acidic (1 mark)
(b) E - Alkaline/basic (1 mark)
[Award 1 mark per correct answer]

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO important digestive functions of the substance secreted in part B.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• It is antiseptic and destroys bacteria/prevents rotting of stomach content
• Changes the pH of the stomach from alkaline to acidic
• Changes disaccharides into monosaccharides
• Activates pepsinogen to form pepsin
• Pepsin changes proteins to peptones
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the role played by part C in the digestion of food in the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: It grinds food into smaller particles for easy digestion / mechanical / physical digestion
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Pigs that are housed inside farrowing pens with cement floors normally show a mineral deficiency. Name the mineral element that is deficient in these pigs.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Iron / Fe
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO deficiency symptoms of the mineral element named in QUESTION 2.2.1 that the pigs will show.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following iron deficiency symptoms:
• Anaemia
• Paleness of mucous membranes
• Listlessness/laziness/fatigue/lethargy
• Laboured/difficult breathing
• Accelerated heartbeat
• Loss of appetite
• Diarrhoea
• Reduced growth
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE method to supplement the mineral element named in QUESTION 2.2.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Any ONE of the following:
• Soil sods
• Injection
• Iron paste/paint/solution
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Name the feed component that is recommended for the optimum growth of pigs.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Protein
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce the purpose of the feed trial above. (Refer to the feed trial diagram showing dry oat hay (8 kg) and dry manure (4,5 kg) in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: To determine the digestibility of the hay / amount of oat hay digested and absorbed
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Classify the feed used in this feed trial.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Roughage
[Award 1 mark — oat hay is a roughage feed]

subQuestions.questionText: Use a formula to calculate the digestibility coefficiency of the feed used in the feed trial above. (Show ALL calculations.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct formula: $DC = \frac{\text{Dry material intake (kg)} - \text{Dry mass of manure (kg)}}{\text{Dry material intake (kg)}} \times 100$
Mark 2: Correct substitution: $= \frac{8 \text{ kg} - 4{,}5 \text{ kg}}{8 \text{ kg}} \times 100$
Mark 3: Correct calculation working
Mark 4: Correct final answer with unit: $= 43{,}75\%$
[Award 4 marks total]

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the substance that could be added to this feed to improve each of the following:
(a) Palatability
(b) Protein content
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Molasses (1 mark)
(b) Urea / biuret (1 mark)
[Award 1 mark per correct answer]

subQuestions.questionText:
A feed has a total digestible nutrient (TDN) content of 80% and a digestible protein content (DP) of 8%. Calculate each of the following:
(a) The % of non-nitrogen substances in the feed (2)
(b) Nutritive ratio (NR) of this feed (use a formula) (3)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) % of non-nitrogen substances (2 marks):
Mark 1: $= 80\% - 8\%$
Mark 2: $= 72\%$

(b) Nutritive ratio (3 marks):
Mark 1: Correct formula: $NR = 1 : \frac{\%TDN - \%DP}{\%DP}$ OR $NR = 1 : \frac{\%\text{ digestible non-nitrogen substances}}{\%\text{ digestible protein}}$
Mark 2: Correct substitution: $1 : \frac{80\% - 8\%}{8\%}$ OR $1 : \frac{72\%}{8\%}$
Mark 3: Correct final answer: $1 : 9$
[Award 5 marks total]

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO components that make up the non-nitrogen content of a feed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Digestible fat / lipids
• Digestible carbohydrates
• Vitamins
• Minerals
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: If a farmer has 150 beef cattle and each requires 5 kg of feed a day, calculate, in tons, the total feed requirement during month 3. (Show ALL calculations.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct formula/setup: Feed required = number of animals × feed/animal/day × number of days = $150 \times 5 \times 30$
Mark 2: Correct working: $= 22\,500 \text{ kg}$ then $\frac{22\,500}{1\,000}$
Mark 3: Correct final answer with unit: $= 22{,}5 \text{ tons}$
[Award 3 marks total]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether there will be enough feed for the cattle during month 3.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Feed will be enough / Yes
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 2.5.2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Feed required is 22 500 kg and feed available is 30 000 kg / there is a surplus of 7 500 kg
[Award 1 mark for a correct reason that compares the figures]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the month with the least shortage of feed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Month 6
[Award 1 mark — feed required = 42 000 kg, feed produced = 40 000 kg, shortage of only 2 000 kg]

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE cost effective strategy to address the shortage of feed during certain months in the table above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Any ONE of the following:
• Storage of feed during months where there is an excess
• Stock reduction / culling
• Controlled calving / change the breeding season
• Planting of seasonal fodder crops
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the feedlot that operates at the highest cost. (Refer to the table showing Feedlot 1 with Output R1 720, Feed cost R600, Other cost R180; Feedlot 2 with Output R1 680, Feed cost R750, Other cost R60.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Feedlot 2
[Award 1 mark — Total cost: Feedlot 1 = R780, Feedlot 2 = R810, so Feedlot 2 has the highest cost]

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the feedlot that operates in the most cost-effective way.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Feedlot 1
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the answer to QUESTION 3.1.2 by referring to the table above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award marks for ONE of the following explanations (worth 2 marks):
• The total cost was the lowest (R780 compared to R810) AND the output was the highest (R1 720 compared to R1 680)
• A greater output for a lower cost
[Award 2 marks for a complete explanation showing both lower cost AND higher output]

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate how each of the structures below helps farm animals to survive adverse environmental conditions:
(a) Shelter
(b) Insulation material
(c) Roofing
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Shelter (1 mark): Has sides for protection against cold winds / reduces wind chill / the enclosed area keeps heat within / insulation
(b) Insulation material (1 mark): Heat can be retained / protection against cold / heat for a longer period of time / cooling effect
(c) Roofing (1 mark): For protection against rain / cold / direct sunlight
[Award 1 mark per correct answer]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify, in the table above, the temperature requirement of broilers at the age of three weeks. (Refer to the table of broiler temperature requirements in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: 25°C
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce, from the table above, the trend of temperature requirements of broilers over a period of 7 weeks.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Temperature requirements decline with increased age
Mark 2: Until it stabilizes from week 5 to 7 (or remains constant from week 5 onwards at 20°C)
[Award 2 marks for full description of the trend]

subQuestions.questionText: Use the data in the table above to draw a line graph showing the temperature requirements of broilers at different ages for the first month of growth.
subQuestions.memoText:
Marking criteria/rubric (award 1 mark each, total 6 marks):
Mark 1: Correct heading (e.g. 'Temperature requirements of broilers at different ages for the first month')
Mark 2: X-axis: correct calibrations and labelling (Age in weeks)
Mark 3: Y-axis: correct calibrations and labelling (Temperature requirements)
Mark 4: Correct units shown (°C and weeks)
Mark 5: Line graph drawn (not bar/other type)
Mark 6: Accuracy — at least 80% correctly plotted

Data to plot (first month only):
Week 1: 35°C
Week 2: 30°C
Week 3: 25°C
Week 4: 20°C

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the part of the handling facility above that has animals inside. (Refer to the illustration of the handling facility in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Holding pen / paddock
[Award 1 mark for either term]

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons why it is important to restrain animals in a crush that is attached to the facility above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• To ensure safety while working with large animals / no harm to the handlers
• To be able to work with animals while they are stable
• To perform specialised practices on animals (AI/dehorning/castration/tattooing/branding/medication/physical examinations)
• Time and labour efficient
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO basic guidelines to be considered when handling cattle.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Keep safety as the main principle in mind
• Cattle should be kept as calm as possible
• Use the correct handling equipment/facilities
• No carrying of sticks/beating/throwing stones
• No shouting/whistling/wild gestures
• Move around slowly/no running around
• Keep animals of the same size/age/sex together
• Separate sick/old/pregnant animals from healthy animals
• Limit the number of people in a facility
• Do not approach animals from behind
• Announce your presence through touch to the animal's front or side
• Let cattle in and out in the same manner / use routine
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Complete the table above by providing the missing information for A, B, C and D. (Refer to the table on diseases that affect farm animals in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Virus (1 mark) — pathogenic agent of Newcastle disease
B - Mastitis (1 mark) — disease causing swollen, hot, painful udder in lactating animals
C - Poultry / cattle / pigs / sheep (1 mark) — animals affected by coccidiosis
D - Fleece contains hard lumps / crusts / scabs on the ears / lips / face / shanks / scrotum / sores on the skin / loss of wool (1 mark) — symptoms of lumpy wool
[Award 1 mark per correct entry]

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO preventative measures to reduce the spread of Newcastle disease.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Timely diagnosis and vaccination against diseases
• Outbreaks must be detected quickly
• Good husbandry must be practiced (housing/nutrition/management)
• Movement of animals should be controlled
• Proper hygiene/sanitation/clean conditions
• Use breeds resistant to diseases
• Quarantine/isolation
• Proper disposal of carcasses
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO financial implications of animal diseases.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Decrease in production / poor quality
• Stock losses / death
• Decrease in income / profit
• Banning of exports / international trade decreases
• Negative impact on food security
• High cost to control / treatment
[Maximum 2 marks]
subQuestions.topic: Animal Protection - Economic Impact of Diseases

subQuestions.questionText:
Write down the letter (A–F) that represents each of the following stages in the life cycle of the parasite in the diagram above:
(a) The larvae that hatches from the egg
(b) The nymph that will feed on the second host
(c) The tick that will feed on the third host
(d) The first host after the larvae stage
(Refer to the diagram of the parasite life cycle in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) B (1 mark) — larvae hatching from the egg
(b) D (1 mark) — nymph that feeds on the second host
(c) E (1 mark) — adult tick feeding on the third host
(d) C (1 mark) — first host after the larvae stage
[Award 1 mark per correct letter]

subQuestions.questionText: Metallic salts can be toxic and poisonous if consumed in excess by farm animals. Precautionary measures should be taken to avoid the risk of poisoning. Indicate TWO symptoms of urea poisoning.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following symptoms of urea poisoning:
• Nervous symptoms / lack of balance / incoordination
• Excessive salivation
• Frequent defecation and urination
• Struggling violently / bellowing
• Bloating
• Tetany / muscular pain
• Breathing difficulty
• Rapid death
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText:
Write down the letter (A–G) of the part in the diagrams above that is associated with EACH of the following:
(a) Site of fertilisation
(b) Where copulation occurs
(c) Maturation of sperm cells
(Refer to Diagram 1 (female reproductive organ with parts C, D, E, F, G) and Diagram 2 (male testis with parts A and B) in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) D (1 mark) — site of fertilisation (oviduct/Fallopian tube)
(b) G (1 mark) — where copulation occurs (vagina)
(c) B (1 mark) — maturation of sperm cells (epididymis)
[Award 1 mark per correct letter]

subQuestions.questionText: Name a membrane in E that is responsible for the implantation of a zygote.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Endometrium
[Award 1 mark — the endometrium is the inner uterine membrane responsible for zygote implantation]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the part in DIAGRAM 1 that performs a function similar to the one performed by A in DIAGRAM 2. Write down only the letter (A–G).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: C
[Award 1 mark — C (ovary in Diagram 1) performs the same gamete-producing function as A (seminiferous tubules/testis in Diagram 2)]

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO congenital defects that may cause sterility in DIAGRAM 2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Cryptorchidism (failure of testes to descend into scrotum)
• Hypoplasia (underdeveloped testes)
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: State the duration of the above cycle in cows. (Refer to the pie chart illustrating the oestrus cycle stages in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: 21 days
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the stage of the oestrus cycle represented by each of the following letters:
(a) B
(b) D
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) B - Di-oestrus (1 mark) — the longest stage, hence the largest segment
(b) D - Oestrus (1 mark) — the standing heat phase
[Award 1 mark per correct stage]

subQuestions.questionText: In the pie chart above, identify the part that represents the stage of high FSH secretion. Write down only the letter (A–D).
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: C
[Award 1 mark — C represents pro-oestrus, the stage of high FSH secretion that stimulates follicle development]

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO practical methods used by dairy farmers to identify the cows in heat.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Heat mount detector
• Tail chalking / tail head marker
• Pedometer
• Chin-ball marker
• Heat observation
• Androgenised females (teaser animals)
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate what happens to the corpus luteum if the cow becomes pregnant.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Corpus luteum persists and continues to secrete progesterone
[Award 1 mark for a complete answer mentioning persistence AND progesterone secretion. Award partial credit if only one aspect is mentioned, depending on marker discretion]

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO factors that regulate mating behaviour in bulls.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Hormonal influences
• Social interaction
• Senses (sight/smell)
• Environmental factors
• Physiological factors
• Previous experience
• Health
• Genetic factors
• Libido
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Name a chemical substance found in the urine of cows in oestrus that stimulates libido in bulls.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Pheromones
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify a reproductive technique to which each of the following statements is applicable:
(a) Production of offspring that are genetically identical to the parent
(b) Needs hormonal treatment
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Cloning (1 mark) — produces genetically identical offspring
(b) Synchronization of oestrus / embryo transfer (1 mark) — both require hormonal treatment
[Award 1 mark per correct answer]

subQuestions.questionText: Define the term embryo transfer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: The transfer of an embryo from a genetically superior female animal (donor)
Mark 2: To the uterus of a genetically inferior female animal (recipient)
[Award 2 marks for a complete definition mentioning donor (superior) AND recipient (inferior/surrogate)]

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO advantages of artificial insemination.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Reduces the exchange of sexually transmitted diseases
• Superior male animal can fertilize more female animals
• Semen from males in other countries can be used
• Quick and economical way to improve the herd
• Valuable tool in assisting with progeny testing
• Semen can be used long after bull's death
• Possible where natural mating is impossible
• No need to buy, keep and maintain expensive bulls
• Inferior bulls can be detected at an early stage and avoided
• AI increases the reproductive and conception rate
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Name a reproductive stage that follows immediately after successful artificial insemination.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Fertilisation
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Give the appropriate term for difficult birth.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Dystocia
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO causes of difficult birth.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Deviation of the head
• Flexion of elbow
• Retention of one or both forelegs
• Hydrocephalus
• Congenital defects/abnormalities/malformed foetus
• Twinning/multiplets
• Posterior/incorrect presentation
• Age of the animal
• Large foetus
• Dead foetus
• Torsion of the uterus
• Uterine inertia/weak contractions/labour
• Prolonged gestation period
• Size of the pelvic area
• Poor body condition
• Incomplete cervical dilation
• Vaginal tear/injuries
• Diseases
[Maximum 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Name a hormone responsible for the relaxation of the cow's muscles before parturition.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Relaxin
[Award 1 mark]

subQuestions.questionText: Give THREE noticeable behavioural changes in a cow which is about to give birth.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any THREE of the following:
• Isolation / nesting behaviour
• Stops eating / lack of appetite
• Making bellowing noises
• Restlessness / signs of discomfort because of pain
• Urinates and defecates often
[Maximum 3 marks]

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the hormones responsible for each of the following:
(a) Milk production
(b) Milk release
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Milk production - Prolactin (1 mark)
(b) Milk release - Oxytocin (1 mark)
[Award 1 mark per correct answer]

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate TWO stimuli that enhance the release of milk.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for any TWO of the following:
• Touching/washing/massaging of the udder
• Sound of the milking machine
• Presence/sight of the calf / suckling of the calf
• Presence of the milker
